title: observability(api): propagate request-id and trace; structured logs + per-endpoint metrics tags (openai compat)
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Context: Customers and internal SREs have asked for consistent request-scoped observability across the API surface including streaming endpoints and the OpenAI compatibility layer. Currently request IDs are generated inconsistently between the gateway, streaming runtime, and the OpenAI-compat handlers which makes tracing and incident postmortems noisy. Motivation: this PR standardizes request id / trace propagation, enriches structured logs with request metadata, and tags per-endpoint metrics so dashboards and SLO alerts can reliably filter by route. What this PR does: 1) Canonical request id middleware (X-Request-ID / X-Amzn-Trace-Id / traceparent): adds middleware that picks an incoming request-id if present, falls back to generated UUIDv4, and injects the same id into streaming frames, internal GRPC calls, and outbound logs. 2) Trace propagation: propagate W3C traceparent through internal RPCs and include trace id in logs and metrics labels. 3) Structured JSON logger: add json_logger with stable fields: timestamp, level, service, env, request_id, trace_id, endpoint, route, model, client_id, duration_ms, error (if any). Replaces key ad-hoc log.Printf sites in gateway + openai compat layer. 4) Per-endpoint metrics tags: ensure metric["requests_total"], metric["latency_ms"] include labels endpoint and route (e.g. "/v1/chat/completions", "/v1/embeddings") so Grafana panels and SLOs can filter reliably. 5) Streaming stability fixes: ensure request_id and tracecontext are carried on streaming frames (SSE and HTTP chunked), fix a race where stream cancellation would drop the request id header on proxied requests by copying headers before context cancellation. 6) OpenAI compatibility: map OpenAI-style header X-OpenAI-Request-ID to internal request_id and ensure response header is preserved for upstream users. Backwards compatibility: existing clients' X-Request-ID or X-OpenAI-Request-ID continue to be respected; if none provided behavior unchanged (server generates id). Migration notes: dashboards should switch to use the request_id and trace_id fields in logs and to the new endpoint tag on metrics. Linear / ENG tickets: ENG-7142 (observability workstream), ENG-7150 (streaming request lifecycle). Security: no changes to auth. Testing: added unit tests for middleware, integration test for streaming frame header propagation, and e2e test that verifies metrics tags emitted. Checklist: - [x] Core middleware implemented and unit-tested - [x] Streaming frames carry request id/trace - [x] OpenAI compat header mapping - [x] Structured logger implemented and wired - [x] Metrics tagging added and e2e tested - [x] Updated docs (console observability README) - [x] Added migration note to release notes Related PRs: #65217 #72103 (observability tracing work), #56201 (streaming compat)

release_notes:
- Added consistent request_id propagation across API gateway, streaming runtime, and OpenAI compatibility layer.
- Structured JSON logs now include request_id and trace_id for easier searching and incident investigation.
- Metrics include per-endpoint tags for accurate SLO filtering.
- Streaming endpoints now preserve request_id/tracecontext across frames and proxied calls.
notes_for_sre: SRE: dashboards updated to use `endpoint` metric tag and log fields `request_id`/`trace_id`. If you see missing request_id for some legacy clients, check for proxies that strip X-Request-ID or X-OpenAI-Request-ID headers. Use new integration test harness to reproduce streaming cancellation races.
performance_notes: Minor overhead from adding request_id and trace propagation and structured logging; measured <1% p99 latency impact in synthetic perf runs. Metrics tagging adds cardinality but uses a constrained set of endpoint values to avoid high-cardinality explosion.
